text:
Tampa Bay arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, having rallied from two goals down to beat Minnesota 4-3 in overtime last night for a third straight win (4-0-1 in their last five). Winnipeg is 2-3-0 in its last five after a 6-2 win over Vancouver, where Viggo Björck picked up his first NHL point. The Jets are still without Josh Morrissey (wrist), so Mario Ferraro has moved in beside DeMelo and Neal Pionk has taken a spot on the first power-play unit. TBL won the first meeting 6-4 on Oct 29, a game it deserved to win 76% of the time (the share of simulated replays of every shot that it wins).

Our numbers favor the Lightning, who have taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, against 47% for Winnipeg. The model has TBL at 3.47 expected goals tonight and WPG at 2.89. Tampa's power play creates 0.82 expected goals a game, and Winnipeg's penalty kill allows 0.90, the matchup to watch. In net, projected starters Andrei Vasilevskiy (-0.51 goals saved above expected this season, +23.15 last year) and Stuart Skinner (+1.07, then +5.96) are both near .885.

Kyle Connor is our top Jet at 43% to score, and Jake Guentzel (40%) and Brandon Hagel (39%) lead Tampa. Nikita Kucherov is 84% for a point. One under-the-radar pick: Pontus Holmberg, a third-line forward with 2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 18% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
